R1NUOX6Q9SX861.fecha: Calificado en Estados Unidos el 23 de febrero de 2026
R1NUOX6Q9SX861.texto:
Let’s start with the obvious: bitter is an understatement. If you are expecting something mild, herbal, or even remotely pleasant, this product will surprise you. The taste of the Serene Herbs Organic Black Seed Oil Bitters Liquid is intensely sharp, earthy, and lingering. The bitterness hits immediately and stays with you for a while. That said, the strength of the flavor actually signals what many people want from a supplement like this—something that feels potent and natural rather than overly processed.

The product itself appears to be made with straightforward ingredients, featuring black cumin seed extract (Nigella sativa) in a liquid bitters form. For those familiar with traditional remedies, black seed products are known for their bold flavor profile, and this one certainly delivers on authenticity. It tastes very much like a concentrated herbal extract rather than something designed to be masked with sweeteners or additives.

Despite the intense flavor, the product does seem to do what it is intended to do. After using it consistently, I noticed that it felt like a strong digestive tonic, which is often why people reach for bitters in the first place. Because it is in liquid form, it is also easy to take quickly or mix with water if the taste is too strong on its own.

Serene Herbs’ Black Seed Bitters Herbal Detox is packed with health and excludes unnecessary ingredients.

The ingredient list is extensive and packed with only healthy ingredients. Black seed is the first ingredient, which is a step ahead of some of the other brands out there that advertise one thing and have it last on the list (something I reviewed recently was like that). I use several of these ingredients on a regular basis for detox and antioxidants. The ingredients are thoughtfully selected toward this purpose.

I REALLY like that there are not fillers. I’m disgusted by how many healthy products are ruined by tons of sugar, preservatives, or other ingredients that are entirely unnecessary for flavor or building product bulk. I’d rather have something like this that I can use to make my own palatable concoction (or not mix it).

Some of the info on the product page is misleading and inconsistent with the product label. For instance, the webpage claims, “Approved in FDA-registered” contrasted to other brands that have “No FDA lab approval.” If that information is true, then it must be for the brand, not this product. There’s no FDA approval on the product, with the only FDA mention being the typical “This statement has not been evaluated by the FDA….” The “Backed by 3,000+ 5-star reviews” is another pain point for me, especially given the current 4.4-star rating on Amazon with only 26 reviews. If that data is coming from somewhere else, then it should be honestly represented. I think clarity and honesty in representing the product and information needs to improve.

The flavor is awful, and the producers recommend chasing it with another drink. I appreciate the honesty there!

All in all, I think it’s a great product, given the ingredient list and absence of fillers. I wish only that they would improve their product listing to be more clear and honest.

Just wanted to get that out of the way so that anyone who gets this isn't put off by the smell. Since I started taking it I felt better, lighter with a sense of freshness, for lack of the perfect word. I definitely feel that this is effective in its detox efforts, as I noticed a change the very next day after the first dose. I feel like I have more pep in my step, so to speak, and there's definitely been an improvement in digestion and gut health.
